references.text: The experts in the law rejected God's plan for themselves – here we see who these experts in the law (νομικοί) are that Jesus now confronts. [ref:Luk 7:30|Luke 7:30]
Jesus' response to the expert in the law's objection follows immediately, where he pronounces three woes specifically directed at the experts in the law. [ref:Luk 11:46-52|Luke 11:46-52]

The preceding woes against the Pharisees that the expert in the law reacts to – he perceives that Jesus' accusations against the Pharisees also strike at the experts in the law. [ref:Luk 11:42-44|Luke 11:42-44]
Matthew's parallel where Jesus pronounces woes over the scribes and Pharisees, including both groups in the same accusation. [ref:Matt 23:13-15|Matthew 23:13-15]

A parallel in Matthew where Jesus directs similar accusations against the scribes and Pharisees about building the prophets' graves, which corresponds to what Jesus says to the experts in the law in Luke. [ref:Matt 23:29-36|Matthew 23:29-36]
Another expert in the law (νομικός) who confronts Jesus – here too with the address "Teacher" (Διδάσκαλε), showing the same approach from this group. [ref:Luk 10:25|Luke 10:25]
Jesus speaks to the experts in the law and the Pharisees on another occasion, which shows the close connection between these two groups. [ref:Luk 14:3|Luke 14:3]
An expert in the law (νομικός) asks Jesus a question – this shows that the experts in the law were a recognizable group who related to Jesus, often in confrontation. [ref:Matt 22:35|Matthew 22:35]
